title: Release smoke test: install and run every published release file after a cut (incl. the Intel half of the macOS universal build)

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What's missing.** Tests cover each platform's *code* (post-merge gate on Linux, the release gate at a cut, Windows quick checks on two Windows boxes), but nothing checks the *packages* `release.yml` publishes. The 0.26.0 release has 11 files: Linux `.tar.gz`, AppImage, `.deb`, `.rpm`, flatpak, snap, Arch `.pkg.tar.zst`, macOS universal `.dmg`/`.zip`, Windows `setup.exe`/`.zip`. Of these, only the macOS zip's contents are listed in the workflow (`unzip -l ... | grep`). None is installed or started. A bad `.deb` dependency, a broken flatpak, a missing asset folder in the `.dmg`, or an installer that does not start would ship unnoticed. The **x86_64 half of the macOS universal build never runs anywhere**.

**Proposal (no Actions minutes; collaborator machines):** after `release.yml` publishes a tag, one script downloads every asset, checks `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and on a box of that platform:
- installs/unpacks it the way a user would (AppImage, `.deb`, `.tar.gz` on Linux; `.rpm` and flatpak on an rpm/flatpak box; `.dmg` on a Mac; `setup.exe` silent install on Windows);
- runs `camcraft-cli --version` (must name the tag) and a small headless job: import the bundled example part, generate, post, and compare the posted program with a committed expected output;
- on a Mac, runs the same job a second time under Rosetta (`arch -x86_64`), which exercises the Intel slice of the universal binary (not Intel GPUs, not speed).
Results: one line per file (PASS/FAIL + reason) as a comment on the release PR / the cut's tracking issue.

**Optional, maintainer's call:** a real Intel check on GitHub's `macos-15-intel` runner (the last x86_64 macOS image, supported until about Aug 2027), one short job per cut (about 50 billed minutes at the macOS rate).

**Done means:** after a cut, every published release file has a PASS/FAIL line from an install-and-run check, including the x86_64 macOS slice under Rosetta; a failing file is named before users hit it.

Related: the browser build at `/app/` (separate issue), the release-tier cut runner (#1413).
